title: The $150 piano for Earl Hines
summary: When Earl Hines replaced Scobey, the manager spent $4100 a week on music but bought a $150 piano and painted it black.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And it was ridiculous and I couldn't cure it. Well, finally, the Continental -- Bob did leave for a stretch and they put Earl Hines in. And now, there's a story I want to tell about that. Earl Hines is coming in, we got to get a piano. They had an upright Kimball and it was a gas but now we got to get a grand for Earl, right? Spending $4100 a week on music, got to get a grand. Of course, that included the other gypsy band that was playing in the other room or something.
Okay. You know what that guy did? This genius who was running the club? He found that there was a piano at some

dray house or something that had been standing there for years. He could get it for $150. And he got that $150 piano and had it hauled and tuned and painted black. And I know it was painted black because I followed Earl and the paint came off on my shirt. For a long time I couldn't get rid of it. The paint was still fresh.
And it was a dog. What could you buy for $150? I couldn't get over it. Here's a man spending $4100 on music, and he's going to give the star a $150 piano.
